## Preambles
```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(brms)
library(forcats)
```

## Exercise 1

```{r}
# Gibson & Wu's Github repo is cloned in the working directory
gw <- read.table("NicenboimVasishthPart2/gibsonwu2012data.txt")
#class(gw)

# basic review of the dataset
glimpse(gw)

# n2-only df (sum coding)
gw.n2 <- gw %>%
  filter(region == "headnoun") %>%
  mutate(
    type = fct_relevel(type, "subj-ext", "obj-ext"),
    type_c = if_else(type == "subj-ext", -0.5, 0.5))
head(gw.n2)
```

## Exercise 2

```{r}
summary(gw.n2$rt)
summary(log(gw.n2$rt))
hist(gw.n2$rt)
```

> I choose a **lognormal likelihood** because RTs are strictly positive and typically right-skewed.
And I specify a **Normal(6, 1)** prior for the intercept, reflecting a plausible baseline median RT of approximately 403 ms (=exp(6)) while allowing uncertainty about the intercept.

```{r}
fit_RT <- brm(rt ~ 1 + type_c + (1 + type_c | subj) + (1 + type_c | item),
              data = gw.n2,
              family = lognormal(),
              prior = c(
                prior(normal(6, 1), class = Intercept),
                prior(normal(0, 0.1), class = b, coef = type_c),
                prior(normal(0, 1), class = sigma),
                prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd),
                prior(lkj(2), class = cor)
              ))
posterior_summary(fit_RT, variable = "b_type_c")
```

Following section 5.3.1 in Nicemboim et al., density plots for the prior and posterior distributions of β are provided:

```{r}
sample_b_post <- as_draws_df(fit_RT)$b_type_c
# We generate samples from the prior as well:
N <- length(sample_b_post)
sample_b_prior <- rnorm(N, 0, 0.1)
samples <-
  tibble(sample = c(sample_b_post, sample_b_prior),
         distribution = c(rep("posterior", N), rep("prior", N)))
ggplot(samples, aes(x = sample, fill = distribution)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
```

> A posterior shifted away from zero = the data have updated beliefs;
> A narrower posterior = the data have reduced uncertainty about β.

- Check model convergence and how well it fit

> Model converged very well with Rhat = 1.00 across the board. ESS values look reasonably large enough too.

```{r}
summary(fit_RT)
```

> Although the lognormal likelihood captures the overall right-skewed shape of the observed RT distribution,
posterior predictive checks reveal systematic discrepancies; the model consistently predicts minimum RTs substantially below the observedminimum of 172 ms. 

```{r}
pp_check(fit_RT, type = "dens_overlay", ndraws = 100)
pp_check(fit_RT, type = "stat", stat = "min")
pp_check(fit_RT, type = "stat", stat = "max")
```

## Exercise 3

> The posterior mean effect of extraction type was −0.056 (95% credible interval: 
[−0.147, 0.037]). Since ORCs were coded as +0.5 and SRCS as -0.5, this corresponds to 
~5.4% shorter RTs for ORCs than SRCs (the negative coefficient = the positive factor, ORC, 
gets smaller RTs compared to the negative factor, SRC),contrary to Gibson and Wu's prediction. 
However, CrI includes zero, meaning there is a visible uncertainty about 
the direction of the effect. Thus, the model does not provide convincing evidence 
that ORCs are read more slowly(/fastly) than SRCs.
